headline: Slow-growth stalemate: tariffs creep, debts swell, frontier defaults cluster, nobody fixes anything

events: Ukraine front freezes into a de facto armistice line without a peace treaty; EU sanctions rolled over, reconstruction finance stalls
US extends sectoral tariffs to pharmaceuticals and chips equipment; China answers with rare-earth export licensing tightened for 'unfriendly' end users
Fed trims to 3.25% then pauses as tariff pass-through keeps core inflation near 3%; ECB holds at 2%
AI capex boom continues but hyperscaler margins wobble; two mid-tier AI model labs are absorbed by Big Tech
Ethiopia-style restructurings drag on; Common Framework talks for two more frontier economies open
US presidential election produces divided government; debt-ceiling standoff resolved at the last minute with a two-year suspension
Mild US slowdown (two flat quarters, no NBER recession); global growth dips to 2.3%
Bolivia and Pakistan miss Eurobond payments within six months of each other; IMF programmes take a year to finalise
Commercial-property losses force three regional bank mergers in the US and a Landesbank recapitalisation in Germany
Record heat in South Asia cuts wheat output; India imposes export bans, food inflation spikes in North Africa
Inflation re-accelerates briefly to ~3.6% G20 average on food and freight costs as Red Sea disruptions recur
Border clashes escalate into a months-long armed conflict in the Sahel involving two states and Wagner-successor forces, displacing 2 million
EU adopts a watered-down 2040 target (85% cut with large international credits); CBAM revenues fund little
Japan 10-year yields touch 2.5%; BoJ slows QT and MoF shortens issuance, averting a disorderly sell-off
Back-office and customer-service employment in India and the Philippines falls for the first time as agentic AI matures
COP35 confirms the world is off track for 1.5C; global emissions are roughly 2% below 2025, not 43%
Kenya restructures domestic and external debt after protests topple a finance minister; fourth sovereign crisis of the period
US-China agree a narrow 'guardrails' deal on soybeans, fentanyl precursors and a military hotline, but chip controls widen
France's deficit stuck above 5% triggers a spread spike to 140bp; ECB's TPI is discussed but not activated
Youth unemployment protests in Nigeria, Bangladesh and Morocco; governments respond with fuel subsidies they cannot afford
Global growth settles around 2.7%; US deficit ~6.5% of GDP with net interest exceeding defence spending
Roughly 29% of firms use AI in production; productivity gains visible in software, finance and logistics but not in aggregate statistics
WTO dispute settlement still paralysed; share of world trade between rival blocs down ~10% from 2025
Housing affordability becomes the top issue in elections in Canada, Australia, the UK and Spain; rent caps spread
Gaza ceasefire holds shakily; Iran-Israel tensions simmer without a full war

winners: Connector economies (Vietnam, Mexico, UAE, Morocco) capturing rerouted supply chains
Big Tech and AI infrastructure owners with pricing power
Owners of existing housing and land in supply-constrained cities
losers: Indebted frontier economies in Africa and South Asia facing high rates and aid cuts
Young renters and entry-level white-collar workers in rich countries
Climate-exposed farmers and coastal communities in the tropics
bullets: Nothing collapsed and nothing was fixed: growth averages ~2.6%, below the pre-2020 trend, with fiscal space eroded everywhere
Public debt passes 100% of world GDP; interest bills now crowd out investment and social spending in the US, France, UK and Japan
Four sovereign debt crises in frontier markets resolved slowly and painfully, with China and bondholders arguing over comparability
Trade runs on blocs and 'friend-shoring' bilateral deals; tariff levels are slightly higher than 2026 and treated as permanent
AI is everywhere in large firms but diffusion is uneven; ~38 million jobs displaced globally, mostly absorbed slowly into lower-paid service work
Renewables hit ~42% of electricity but gas and coal persist; warming nears 1.6C and extreme heat is a routine policy problem
Politics is polarised and transactional; trust drifts down, protests flare around cost of living and youth unemployment rather than revolution
wildcard: A Sahel interstate war in 2029 that drew in Gulf and Russian-linked mercenary forces and triggered a major migration wave toward North Africa and Europe
image_description: In a sweltering 2031 Lagos evening, a young graduate rides a solar-charged e-okada delivering parcels routed by an AI dispatch app, passing a half-finished Chinese-financed rail viaduct and a billboard advertising visa lotteries for Gulf construction jobs.
